sections.html:
One office handles appraisal, assessment, ownership records and tax collection. It sits in the David R. Sandifer Administration Building, 30 Government Center Drive, Bolivia, NC 28422. The main number is 910-253-2829. For relief programs call 910-253-2811 on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m.

The tax office page on the county website links to tax bills, property record cards, certifications, the foreclosure list and land records. If you cannot pay a bill in one payment, the collections division offers a payment plan. Ask before the balance is late.

sections.h2: Housing and growth in Brunswick County
sections.html:
Brunswick County has grown fast. Population is 174,702 as of July 2025, up 27.8% from 136,695 in the April 2020 base. There are 116,023 housing units, and 84.6% are owner-occupied. The median home value is $349,800 and median gross rent is $1,351. Builders took out 4,457 permits in 2025, and each new house or addition can change a parcel's value before the next reappraisal.

Nineteen towns and villages levy their own rates, including Bolivia, Northwest, Leland, Navassa, Shallotte, Southport, Oak Island, Holden Beach, Ocean Isle Beach, Sunset Beach, Caswell Beach and Bald Head Island. The town where your parcel sits decides which town rate is added to the county rate.

The county levies 0.3420, or 34.20 cents per $100 of value, and that rate is the same for 2024, 2025 and 2026. It was 0.485 in 2022 and fell to 0.342 in 2023, the year of the last countywide revaluation.

sections.h2: The 2027 revaluation and how to appeal
sections.html:
All parcels will be valued at market and in their condition on January 1, 2027. A building that is unfinished on that date is appraised at its percentage of completion.

New value notices are scheduled for February and March 2027. Compare yours with the record card and look for mistakes in the property data. An appeal has two stages:

  • Informal review: from January until the board of equalization and review convenes, the tax assessor can adjust a value when the facts support it.
  • Formal appeal: after the board convenes, it holds the authority, and owners or their representatives normally present their case in person.

Once the board has convened, any new appeal is treated as formal. After adjournment it is untimely and generally waits for the next year, and a win does not reach back to earlier years. G.S. 105-322 puts the board's first meeting between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May, with a December 1 finish in a reappraisal year. Beyond that sits the Property Tax Commission, which hears appeals filed within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

The due date is September 1. Nothing accrues until after January 5, or the next business day when that date lands on a weekend. This year's bills went out in mid-August, and paying by January 5, 2027 avoids interest.

From January 6 to February 1 a late bill carries 2%. After that it grows by three-fourths of a percent every month or fraction of a month. Mailed checks count as on time by postmark. A prepayment discount is possible when the board sets a schedule by May 1, so ask whether this year has one.

The tax claim attaches as of the January 1 listing date, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure suit.

The county lists four programs. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, can claim the elderly or disabled exclusion on their permanent home if income stays under $38,800 for 2026. The county subtracts $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is larger.

  • Disabled veteran exclusion: a flat $45,000 comes off the appraisal with no age or income test, and an unmarried surviving spouse may claim it too.
  • Homestead circuit breaker: yearly tax cannot exceed 4% of income, or 5% when income is over the limit but within 150% of it. The overage is deferred and carries a lien.
  • Present-use value: farm, horticultural or forest land that qualifies is taxed on what it produces rather than on market value.

If the owner dies, transfers the property or moves out, three years of deferred circuit breaker tax plus interest come due, so a sale triggers that bill. Use the state application form and file it with the county tax office, preferably in January. Filings are taken through June 1.

sections.h2: Taxes and a Brunswick County house sale
sections.html:
By county resolution, a deed must be stamped by the tax office before the Register of Deeds will record it. The stamp shows that taxes, fees and assessments are paid.

To learn what is owed, ask for a Tax Certification under G.S. 105-361. Owners, attorneys and other interested persons can request one. It lists local tax liens, any deferred taxes, fire fees and assessments the office must collect, so ask for it early.

The seller also sends the register the deed tax, $1.00 for every $500 of consideration, before the deed is filed.

sections.h2: Before you list a Brunswick County house
sections.html:
Get your property record card from the county site and read it line by line: square footage, bedroom count, outbuildings. Then order a Tax Certification so you know about liens, deferred taxes, fire fees and assessments before an offer comes in.

If you receive relief, ask the relief line at 910-253-2811 what will come due at closing. A buyer's attorney will see the stamp requirement, so have the tax office stamp ready ahead of the closing date.

sections.h2: If taxes go unpaid: the county auction
sections.html:
A parcel with unpaid taxes may be sold at auction on the courthouse steps in Bolivia, whatever the weather. The high bidder puts down 5% right away, by cash, certified or cashier's check or money order. The county offers no financing.

Then a 10-day upset period opens, and every raise must top the prior bid by 5% or $750, whichever is greater. The winner gets a week after notice to pay the balance and is issued a commissioner's deed. A homeowner can still sell and pay the taxes at closing while the process is pending, so call the collections division early if you are behind.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the Brunswick County Tax Office?
faqs.a: Call 910-253-2829 for the Tax Office or 910-253-2811 for relief programs. The office is at 30 Government Center Drive in Bolivia.

faqs.q: What is the county tax rate in Brunswick County?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.3420 for 2024, 2025 and 2026, with town or district rates added where they apply.

faqs.q: When does the next Brunswick County revaluation take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027, with notices scheduled between February and March 2027. The prior revaluation was effective January 1, 2023.

faqs.q: Is there a grace period on late Brunswick County tax bills?
faqs.a: Not after January 5. Interest begins the next day, and the collections division can arrange a payment plan if you call before the deadline.

faqs.q: Do sellers need a tax stamp before recording in Brunswick County?
faqs.a: Yes. By county resolution the tax office must stamp a deed before the Register of Deeds records it, which confirms taxes, fees and assessments are settled.
